2. If you can't kill her without it, to trade ultimates (hers has a much longer cooldown).
3. After hers, which means you would have had the damage to kill her if she hadn't used it, or you successfully baited it.
-If you’re confident, you can preemptively cast your R so that the damage hits at the end of her ultimate.
-Between levels 6 and 12, Kayle's ultimate has a 40-second longer cooldown than yours. Play around the timing when she doesn’t have her ultimate if you want to kill her.
"-Kayle is very powerful at level 1 but much weaker between levels 2 to 5.
-If Kayle lets you push at level 1, try to slow push the wave and call your jungler for a dive when the wave is under her tower, especially if she doesn’t have Teleport. A 1-for-1 trade will be extremely worth it if she doesn’t have Teleport, and generally fine if she does.
-Likewise, if you can push the wave that gets you to level 6, it’s easy to dive her with the advantage of your ultimate.
-At level 6, you win all-ins if you can get into melee range without losing too much HP.
-Be careful, Kayle outscales you. It's in the mid game where you are most able to make a difference."

-Choose your summoners based on your preference.
-Pay attention to his positioning in teamfights; Kennen is very strong at turning a teamfight with a good flank.
"-Be careful of his empowered auto attacks.
-The matchup is quite difficult early; survive and look for opportunities to take a trade if he overextends."

-Your W can help you tank his W, but you can also disengage when he uses it and fight him when it's on cooldown.
-Kled is a very good roamer. Be aware of this and make sure to ping your team quickly when he is about to roam.
-If you want to kill him, save some burst to finish him off when he loses his mount (usually Ignite + ultimate, but sometimes this isn't enough).
-Kled is very easy to chase when he doesn't have his mount.
"-Kled is a very powerful early game champion who tends to scale poorly. Be careful not to die early because Kled snowballs very well.
-Be cautious; Kled has a very good dive setup (especially on a wave crash at level 3 with Ignite).
-Garen’s W is quite effective against Kled’s burst, but without it, you are quite vulnerable.
-If everything goes well in the early game, you will have much more impact than him in the mid and late game."

-His Qs are quite easy to bait/dodge.
-Similar to Kled, keep some burst for when he ultimates you (often ult + ignite is not enough, so save your cooldowns even if you have to endure his hits until he ultimates).
-Be careful, K'Santé has a very good kit to pull you under his tower or push you out of yours.
"-The matchup depends on the skill level of the K'Santé. A good K'Santé can be problematic if he spaces well and doesn't ult recklessly.
-Don't let him ult you when your cooldowns are down, or he will kill you.
-In general, be mindful of his Q3 timings.
-One of Garen's main strengths in this matchup is his ability to control K'Santé in teamfights."

-His E does not affect the number of spins of your E.
-Be careful, his ultimate provides a very good setup for ganks.
-If he plays with Comet, dodge it with the movement speed from your Q.
-Black Cleaver is an excellent item against Malphite.
-Try to start trades with W-AA-E-Q.
-Don't stay grouped with your team in teamfights.
"-You can try to abuse him in the early game.
-Remember to ping if Malphite roams; with one R mid, he can turn the game around.
-There's not much else to say other than he's a big and sturdy rock; the matchup is quite boring."

-The width of his Q is smaller at the beginning than at the end. You can use this tip to dodge them more easily during an all-in.
-Ideally, don't stand in the minions that Mordekaiser wants to farm to avoid his Qs, but sometimes it can be useful to avoid taking the crit damage from his Q.
-When your jungler ganks, use your silence just before Mordekaiser realizes he needs to ult so that he gets bursted, and even if he ults, he will be low HP.
-QSS no longer works against Mordekaiser (so don't buy the item).
"-With Conqueror, it is generally possible to kill Mordekaiser in an all-in at level 2 if you manage to dodge his grab, assuming he takes it as his second spell.
-Dodge his E.
-The matchup is quite skill-dependent pre-6 but still slightly in Mordekaiser's favor. Try to dodge his spells and punish him when he doesn't have them (especially when his shield is down, he is very vulnerable).
-Post-6, the matchup becomes more difficult and really depends on your ability to dodge his spells.
-Be careful not to overextend in the lane, or you risk dying if you end up in melee range with him knowing he has his ultimate."

-Generally, save your Q to counter his slow.
-Be careful, under his ultimate, he can 1v1 you much more easily; try to wait it out.
-Be cautious when using your ultimate if he hasn't used his yet (unless he is silenced).
-Avoid letting him free farm if you don't get anything in return.
"-Try to abuse him early, whether by playing aggressively, freezing the wave, or calling your jungler for a dive.
-He will gradually outscale you, but your ultimate remains a good tool to control him in teamfights.
-The matchup largely depends on the skill level of the Nasus player; it is difficult to prevent a good Nasus with Fleet Footwork from free farming."

-Focus on dodging his Q when he throws it from a distance.
-Olaf is much weaker when his axe is far from him.
-Make sure to account for his W (shield) if you want to ult him.
"-Be careful not to engage in prolonged fights against Olaf; he can easily chase you down the lane.
-Garen's ultimate and Ignite are problematic tools for Olaf; using them well can easily prevent Olaf from playing effectively.
-The lane is a bit challenging, but you have a significant scaling advantage."

-You can silence him to prevent him from using his second R.
-His W (the breath) procs a passive mark if the last tick hits you. During an all-in, get on top of him and move behind him when he uses W. Generally, try to move around him to increase the chance of him missing his spells.
-Be wary of his Q R E R W combo, which is extremely powerful post-6. Be cautious if you are at half health and get hit by a Q.
-Ornn's ultimate allows him to engage from very far away. Be very careful as his gank setup post-6 is huge. Similarly, remember to ping his roams as they can be devastating.
"-Before level 6, the matchup is quite skill-dependent and turns in Ornn's favor when he buys items (thanks to his passive).
-Post 6, the matchup becomes a bit more playable for you because Ornn has no sustain and your passive starts to become really effective, allowing you to take increasingly worthwhile trades.
-However, Ornn outscales you (mainly due to his passive), so the mid game is the best time for you to make a difference, particularly with your map mobility (Ornn is relatively immobile).
-The matchup is generally quite boring. If there's a moment you can make a difference, it's between levels 6 and 13, whether through roams or solo kills. Otherwise, farm well and manage your waves carefully."

-Remember to ping your team when Pantheon can ult.
-Don't get baited by his E; it can even block the damage from your ult (unless you flash behind him just before Pantheon takes the damage from your ult).
"-The matchup is really difficult in the early game; you need to endure the laning phase, punish him if he misplays his trades, and make a difference in the midgame.
-Focus on using your W to block his combo or empowered Q; the matchup heavily relies on this.
-You have the scaling advantage."

-You can step on her shield to deny it.
-To avoid getting poked too much, you can back off when her passive is up; she will have to use it to farm anyway.
-You can also bait her Q by pretending to move towards her.
-Be very careful with your positioning in lane; if she stuns you against a wall, you'll take a huge trade. If that happens, make sure to use your W to block her stun.
-Be cautious, Poppy has a good setup for diving.
"-Poppy is a very strong laner; she is hard to kill and has very good damage.
-You have the scaling advantage."

-Be careful, her E cancels your Q and her blind cancels your R.
-Quinn is squishy and has low damages in early game
-Quinn can return to lane very quickly with her ult; don't get caught off guard or you could lose a lot.
-It's easy to kill Quinn by blocking her close to a wall so her E doesn't push her away from you
-Tabis = OP 
-You don't really have the chance to kill her in lane unless she makes a mistake. Focus on farming and be sure to signal her roams as much as possible. You have better scaling.

-Be careful when using your ult if he hasn't used his yet (unless he is silenced).
-It is possible to build Plated Steelcaps in this matchup.
"-Renekton is quite powerful in the early-mid game, but your kit is strong against him, especially if you can use W and E to counter his stun.
-You can try to take trades when you have your W, but be mindful of his fury bar.
-If you have the lead, you can prevent him from hitting your creeps to stop him from building fury.
-The matchup can be a bit tough before the first item, but it becomes easier afterward if you don't fall too far behind. You have the scaling advantage."

-Be mindful of the regeneration from his W, which can easily catch you off guard.
-This is one of the rare matchups where Plated Steelcaps are viable, as they are very strong against a burst champion who relies on auto attacks, but they are not mandatory.
-Be cautious when placing wards in bushes, as Rengar can leap onto them.
"-Play away from bushes and try to play a freeze near from his tower or yours
-Be careful before level 6; Rengar is very powerful during this time, so don't get caught off guard.
-After level 6, you will start to gradually win the matchup."

-You can use your Q at the same time as her third Q.
-While under E, it is possible to move behind her to dodge her Q.
"-The lane matchup relies heavily on how well you can space her and play around her cooldowns.
-The matchup also depends significantly on the skill level of the Riven player; the higher the elo, the more the matchup favors her, and vice versa at lower elo.
-Be careful of his damage in the first levels
-Be very careful of her burst at level 6, especially if she has Ignite.
-You have the scaling advantage with Phase Rush, and the late game is more difficult with Conqueror."

-Rumble cannot back off and use his Q at the same time.
-Rumble deals more damage in the red zone (50%-100% of his heat gauge) and has empowered auto attacks when he overheats, so be mindful of that.
"-The matchup is really tough early; endure the lane until level 11/first item, when the matchup will be more in your favor.
-It is possible to kill him at level 6 if he makes a mistake (overextends with low health, takes a tower shot, etc.), but be careful not to get one-shot.
-You have the scaling advantage."

-If you want to trade with her, remove her passive first (it works a bit like Bone Plating but with a shorter cooldown).
-During a trade, back off before she can proc her 4 passive marks and her stun.
-Be wary of her high one-shot potential at level 6, especially if she has Ignite.

-Try to preemptively use your W + E or just W before his E.
-Be careful, when he is low on health, he regenerates very quickly even during a fight. This is why taking a trade that leaves you both below 50% HP is not worth it, as he will sustain faster.
-Without his W, Sett is much more vulnerable.
-If Sett ults you during your E, your E remains active during his R.
-Try to use your R only if he is silenced, after his W, or in a team fight. You can use the ult as a last resort to surprise him if it's your only hope
"-Generally, try to take only short trades.
-Trades against Sett are winnable as long as you make sure to never take his W charged with true damage.
-Be careful, Sett has a very good dive setup.
-Stop trading with him once he is at mid-health if you can't finish him off.
-Usually, look to disengage quickly after trading with him.
-Make sure not to give him a good setup for his R in teamfights."

-You can start with E to win if he trades with you in your creeps at level 1, but starting with Q is also a good option.
-Don't stay between his sword and him, or he will get a boosted Q and reduce his passive's (shield) cooldown when he uses Q.
-Try to use W and E to counter his taunt.
-Remember to ping when he reaches level 6 and remind your team there's a Shen when they want to engage in a fight.
-When he looks to ult, try to move forward or pressure him to prevent the teleport or force him to teleport under bad conditions.
-If he teleports, push the tower and take plates (basically avoid backing during this timing).
-Be mindful of his shields, which can prevent him from dying to ignite at the last moment, for example.
"-Before level 6, the matchup favors Shen; he will win trades if he lands his taunt.
-Post 6, you win trades if you dodge his E, and it will be to your advantage if you can use W and E to counter his E.
-Try to take long trades; after he uses his burst, Shen isn't very threatening until his next Q.
-You have the scaling advantage, but he is not weak in the early/mid game either."

-Avoid chasing him too much.
-You can use your Q during his flip.
-The matchup depends a lot on how the Singed player plays. In a pure 1v1, you have the advantage if you play correctly. That's why he usually won't look for a fight and will instead try to impact the map or proxy to get more resources than you. You can also proxy if you are confident.

-You can cancel his Q with your silence, but his cooldown will be reset to 2 seconds.
-Be careful if Sion is playing with Phase Rush; he can easily chase you down in his passive if you are in melee range.
-Try to start trades with AA + E or just E to maximize your damage.
-When he tries to escape, position yourself in a way that prevents him from ulting out.
-Sion is very weak in the early game but scales quite well and quickly through his W passive. Try to abuse him early, either by killing him or setting up a good wave.

-Using W against Skarner's ultimate is useless in a 1v1.
-You can cancel his E with Garen's silence.
-Be careful, Skarner can easily pull you under his tower from very far away.
-Skarner has a very good gank setup.
-Skarner can easily drag you down the lane with all his slows.
"-Before level 6, it is possible to abuse him during his cooldowns especially with conqueror, but it becomes much harder after his first back.
-Be mindful of his potential flanks through walls in teamfights."

-Your Q cancels his W; during a gank, save it for the moment he tries to escape with it.
-Your E continues to deal damage even if he eats you.
-Don't use your W when he ults you; it's completely useless.
-Be careful of his Q, which allows him to regenerate a significant amount of HP if it hits you.
-When he uses his W out of your vision, you hear a sound, giving you time to prepare to dodge.
"-The early game against Tahm Kench is really tough. Stay behind your creeps to avoid getting hit by his Q.
-Be cautious of his ultimate, which is quite powerful in 1v1s in the early game.
-Endure the laning phase; you have the scaling advantage."

-Be careful, Teemo can hide anywhere, especially at level 1 and when you are low on health.
-Avoid going into bushes and straying from the minion path to avoid his mushrooms.
-Be cautious when your jungler ganks; the 2v1 can quickly go wrong because of his mushrooms.
"-Like most ranged matchups, you need to endure the early game and punish him if he overextends.
"

-Be careful, Trundle has a very good gank setup.
-You generally can't fight him once he ults you; flee and try to wait it out if you can.
-Avoid building tank items against Trundle; he can easily reduce your resistances with his ult and can just ignore you while hitting the tower in a side lane.
"-Don't take long trades; retreat quickly after your combo, especially when he uses his R.
-Trundle is a very good split pusher; be mindful of this."

-You can surprise Tryndamere with your ultimate by using it at the same time as a tower shot.
-Tryndamere is much weaker with his rage at a minimum. If you have the advantage, you can prevent him from charging it with a good freeze (very situational).
-Be mindful of his Q's regeneration when you want to ult him.
"-You are not really in danger pre-6 if you use your W correctly. You should be able to handle trades but won't be able to kill him due to his sustain.
-Tryndamere is a split pusher; try to neutralize him in the side lane.
-You are more useful than him in 5v5 team fights.
"

-Be careful at level 1, he will try to E you. Avoid it, or you will take a heavy trade.
-Urgot has almost no sustain.
-You can easily bait his E
-You can buy Warden's mail if Urgot becomes too problematic; the item is strong against him and will considerably reduce his damage. The same goes for Plated Steelcaps.
-The further you progress in the game, the more you can run at him whenever you have your W to take a trade. Still, be cautious of his legs (passive), which deal significant damage. Dodge his E if possible, and you will win your trades.

-Her E has a 20-second cooldown early; if you want to all-in, you can do it in two phases.
-You can hide in the lane bushes early to force her to ward them, making her more easily gankable.
-Avoid building too many tank items.
"-Endure the early game while trying to take as little damage as possible when you step up to farm.
-Watch for any mistakes; if she dashes in far from her tower post-6, you can ghost and run her down for an all-in, at least forcing her to use Flash.
-You don't have the advantage in the early or late game, so try to make a difference in the mid game. Remember, picking Vayne top is good against Garen but not necessarily against or with every composition."

-Back off when his Q is charged.
-Be mindful of his regen; a 1v1 can quickly turn in his favor.
-The matchup is quite boring; he can't really kill you and vice versa pre-6. After level 11, the matchup will start to slightly turn in your favor. Punish him if he overextends towards you. Just be cautious of his potential to one-shot you with ult + ignite.

-Use your W and E to counter his stun.
-If he marks you with his W, he can heal a significant amount if he hits you with it again. Back off before he can use W a second time, or you will likely lose the trade.
-Be careful when using your ultimate; if he ults at the same time, he will regenerate HP, making your ultimate much less effective.
-Volibear has a very good setup for diving, whether solo or with his jungler. Place wards accordingly (tri-bush, red side/bush between river and blue, blue side) and avoid staying under your tower with low health, as he won't hesitate to dive you.
"-Dodge his E (it's predictable and deals a lot of damage, so make sure not to get hit by it).
-Trades are played a lot on whether he manages to put his stun + E combo on you, try to play only short stealthy trades based on Q E while moving back
-In this matchup, it's possible to win the early game, but any mistake can allow Volibear to easily snowball, especially with his solo dive potential via his ultimate.
-The matchup improves slightly over time but 1v1 remains in Volibear's favor."

-Warwick is the ultimate champion who never dies in trades. His regen is boosted when he is low on life, so avoid getting baited.
-Be careful, Warwick often plays with Barrier (and he can activate it during your silence), so don't get caught off guard.
-Taking an even trade against Warwick is rarely worth it.
-Be cautious, in 2v2s and even 2v1s, Warwick is very strong and can easily turn the situation around.
"-The matchup really depends on the skill level of the Warwick. A very good Warwick is almost immortal in lane (especially if he has Barrier), but he is not impossible to kill if he plays poorly (the difficulty lies in distinguishing between a bait and a mistake).
-Before level 6, the matchup is very difficult, so prefer to play safe early.
-Obviously, do not take extended trades against him; you will surely lose after using your burst.
-After the laning phase, Warwick becomes weaker and you have much better scaling."

-If he uses his W (creates a clone) during your Q, your Q will still hit him.
-In an all-in, consider using Ignite early or during the silence to avoid using it on the clone and to be able to see him if he uses his W.
"-Be careful at level 1 when he uses his E; he gets an attack speed boost which allows him to win the trade.
-From level 3 onwards, the matchup is quite skill-dependent. You will win if you manage to use your W against his combo and lose if he successfully pokes and spaces you with his W when you use your E. It's quite similar post-6 (a matter of spacing), except you will gain the advantage as the game progresses.
-Be very careful of his burst at level 6, which can one-shot you, especially if he plays with Ignite."

-You can use your Q during his tornado when you are in melee range; this can prevent you from getting ulted.
-Yasuo has no escape if he is far from your minion waves.
"-Yasuo is the more difficult version of Yone with less damage and more complex spacing tools. It is rare to find a Yasuo causing as many problems as a Yone until high elo.
-Yasuo is a champion with good DPS, so try to avoid taking long trades.
-Just like with Yone, post-6, everything depends on Yasuo's spacing. If he manages to wait out your E, you will be in a bad position (retreat or you will lose); otherwise, you can kill him or win a good trade.
-Your silence is also very effective for controlling him in teamfights."

-You can use your Q during his third Q if you are in melee range.
-If he dashes in with his Q without hitting you, punish him if you are close to him.

-His ghouls give you stacks for your W; last-hitting them allows you to stack it quickly, but they will reset your passive if they attack you.
-If you are caught in his cage, you have lost the trade. Try to bait or dodge it at all costs.
-Yorick is an excellent split pusher; be very careful as he can quickly create a gap in your base if no one defends against him.

-You can walk on his blobs to make them disappear.
-Be cautious of his monstrous sustain from his blobs (similar to Warwick), don't get baited.
-Be mindful of his passive when you kill him early; if you don't kill his blobs, you can easily get turned on.
-Be careful, Zac has a very good gank setup.
-Be cautious when placing a ward during a trade, he might link his Q with it.
"-A good Zac is hard to kill early, similar to Warwick, as he outsustains you, but you can still take good trades with conqueror
-The matchup heavily depends on the skill level of the Zac player."

Aatrox wins early, but all of his damage comes from landing his Q. Fleet Footwork helps us tremendously here because we’re able to dodge his Q more efficiently. Prioritize getting Phage and boots to help with dodging his Q as well.

Akali's all in potential doesn't come into play until she gets her ultimate. When she hits level six, this matchup becomes incredibly difficult because she's granted two damaging gap closers. Watch closely to her resource bar. Her Q will slow you if you are hit by the tip of it. When it comes to Akali's shroud, Gnar's ultimate is a good tool to push her out of it.

Camille has two gap closers that put Gnar in a huge disadvantage. You have the option to dodge her E with your E, but her E is on a significantly lower cooldown. Dodging her E is extremely vital in this matchup. Her second Q press does true damage, so you want to weave in and out of trades to avoid being hit by this. Prioritize getting Phage and boots to help with dodging her E and W.

Cassiopeia struggles early. She scales really well, so look to make plays in lane. Poke her with your Q. Watch her mana closely because her abilities use a lot of it early. Once she grabs her Tear, expect her to start spamming abilities. Her W grounds, so you can't use your E or Flash in it. You can outplay her R by juking backwards as soon as you see the animation start. It'll only hit you if you're looking at her. Adaptive Helm helps a lot here because of her E spam.
Cho’Gath has no way of closing the gap to you and he has to be very close to you in order to use his R. As long as you are dodging his Q and staying at a distance, you will destroy in this matchup.

This matchup can be easy depending on the summoner spell that Darius takes. If he takes Teleport, you can easily kite him out. If he takes Ghost, you absolutely need to be careful with your E and Flash. Generally, Darius starts trades with his Q and E. Watch for his Q cooldown and go in for trades if he misses you with the outside of it. If his Ghost is down, kiting Darius is extremely easy. Wait until you're level 7 to start trading. This is when Gnar's attack range outranges Darius' E.

Dodging Dr. Mundo’s Q is vital in this matchup. If you are avoiding his Q and are poking when you’re able, you should win this matchup with no issues. Because Dr. Mundo benefits from health items, Mini Gnar's W will shred through him.

Fiora can use her W to prevent your third W stack and your all in. Watch for this cooldown and abuse her when it’s down. Keep an eye on the position of her vitals, as this will be your main source of counterplay. A good tip for this matchup would be to hug the terrain that’s on the same side of her vitals when fighting her so she can’t proc it. Consider rushing Ninja Tabi.

Gnar wins early game over Gangplank. Once Gangplank finishes his Triforce, power starts to shift into Gangplank’s favor. The key to this lane is to dodge his exploding barrels. Avoid all inning as Mega Gnar when Gangplank has his W up because it removes CC. His W is on a long cooldown, so abuse him when he uses it.
Garen’s passive can easily be stopped with Gnar’s Q and AA. Focus on kiting Garen when he attempts to Q in for trades.

Gragas uses a lot of mana early. Abuse this. Gnar also has a lot of options to dodge all of his abilities. Always respect Gragas' R as it's an easy way for him to all-in you. You can Flash to the opposite side of his R as he throws it to be thrown into the opposite direction. Gnar's E can do this too, but it's harder to time.

Hecarim has an insane amount of sustain built into his W. He also has a gap closer on his E and R. You can Flash as soon as his E connects to be thrown into the direction you flashed instead of the direction his E would send you. Hecarim struggles before level 6.

Heimerdinger relies heavily on landing his E on you. When he lands his E, he gets full beam charge on his turrets. Make it your priority to dodge this. Another thing to keep in mind is that his ulted turret can't be displaced with your ult. You're going to get pushed in early, so look for ganks from your jungler. Look for all-in opportunities after you hit level six.

All of Illaoi’s all in potential revolves from her E. Dodging this is extremely vital. If you’re hit, walk back and avoid being hit by her tentacles. Her R will summon an extra tentacle if you get hit by her E. Illaoi’s E has a long animation, so dodging it is easy.

Irelia has so many options to close the gap against you. The key here is to keep an eye on your minions that are low on health. Irelia’s Q will reset if she kills a minion with it. You absolutely have to dodge her E because it applies her mark on you. Overall, you want Irelia to push in this matchup as much as possible. Keep your minion wave close to your tower and ask for ganks.

Jarvan IV is going to be looking to land his E → Q combo on you in lane. Dodging this is key because it's all of his damage. It's fairly easy to do so with Fleet Footwork and your passive. A good Jarvan IV will be able to E → Q → Flash, so keep that in mind. If his ult is down, he has no all-in potential. Abuse him when he has cooldowns.

Jax’s only way to trade with you early is his E, so abuse him when it's on cooldown. A good Jax will E → Q to catch your E, so try to time getting away as soon as you see his E animation. Once Jax finishes his Triforce, he becomes a powerhouse.

Jayce has a lot of damage he can deal at a distance. Avoiding his Q is extremely important. If you’re poked down enough, Jayce will switch to Hammer Stance and all in you. Sadly, it’s nearly impossible to all in Jayce when his E is up. He will knock you back as soon as you E in.

Karma can be a very annoying matchup because of the amount of shields and mobility she can pump out in a short amount of time. Her damage is weak early and she also has issues with mana. Look to all-in her after you hit level 6.

Kayle takes a good while to scale. Assuming both of you are even at level 11, Kayle wins. The gap is huge by level 16, so try your best to end the game before then. With that being said, look to gain leads on her before her power spikes. Poke her down with your Q. Look for all-ins at level six.

Kennen’s Q is his main resource for poke. Keep an eye on how many stacks of his passive he has on you. Once he gets three, you’ll be stunned. His E is a long cooldown and his only way to escape, so abuse him when it’s down. Kennen’s kill potential comes from his R. Sadly, his R animation is instant, so try and play outside of its range and keep note on his Flash cooldown. Mostly, you will see AP Kennen, so consider getting MR, but on the off chance you see AD Kennen, build accordingly.

Kled’s early game is phenomenal if he lands his Q and has his W up, so avoiding this is key. Most Kled players will attempt an all in at level three. Kled is a melee champion, so you can easily poke him down off of Skaarl. Be very careful of Kled remounting. His Q off of Skaarl will give him a big chunk of Courage if he hits you with it. He also gets bonus Courage when he autos champions, turrets, and monsters. Kled is also extremely good at diving because of his passive. If he chooses to go for a dive, Kled will lose turret aggro if he falls off Skaarl because he becomes untargetable for a short time.

Lissandra has a gap closer and plenty of disengage in her kit to allow her to be very safe in lane. You can catch her as she uses her E to get away with Mega Gnar's W and R. Look to all-in when her E is on cooldown.

Lucian's lane pressure makes it almost impossible to win trades as Mini Gnar early. Poke with your Q and play safe until level 6. Watch his E cooldown and look to all-in with Mega Gnar when it's on cooldown.

This matchup is difficult due to Malphite’s passive and E. His passive gives him an insane amount of health and armor. His E also lowers your attack speed, making it very difficult to proc your W. Luckily, Malphite is a melee champion, so we have a little freeway here.
Maokai is a melee champion, so poke him as much as possible. Keep an eye on his mana because his abilities will eat it. The only way he can close the gap is his W, but it’s on a long cooldown.

Mordekaiser is easily kited early. Abuse this. Always respect Mordekaiser's R when he's ahead. Gnar has very limited space to kite in death realm. Mini and Mega Gnar's Q will remain in the realm it was thrown in right before his R connects. Gnar cannot ult Mordekaiser into death realm's wall. Look to all-in based on his W charge and his R cooldown.

Nasus has no way to close the gap against you. Gnar can easily zone him out of stacking his Q because Nasus is a melee champion. Freezing the lane close to your tower is extremely efficient at preventing him from stacking. It also allows for easy ganks since he is immobile.
Nautilus is a very easy matchup because he will be building health items. Mini Gnar's W will shred through him. Gnar also has a lot of options to dodge Nautilus' hook.

Neeko relies heavily on hitting her E. Trade with her when it's on cooldown. She can also disguise herself during roams which can be devasting if you're not aware of it. Her ult's zone will be invisible if she casts it while disguised. Poke with Q and all-in after level 6.
Nocturne has fairly strong lane pressure early. Armor helps here. Once he hits level 6, he will look to all-in you if he's ahead or he'll look to roam. All-in after level 6 if his W his on cooldown.

Olaf's early levels in lane can't be beat. The key to this matchup is to dodge his axes. If he hits one axe, it's extremely easy for him to hit more because of the slow. His Q's cooldown is lowered if he picks his axes back up. Look for trades when he misses his axes. The less health he has, the more attack speed and healing he gets, so be very careful fighting him when he's low. Olaf's R allows him to not be CC'd, so all inning as Mega Gnar is not possible when he has it up.

In this lane, you absolutely have to avoid being hit by his W as it’s his primary source of damage. Once he applies Brittle on you, his next auto will do bonus damage and knock you back. Ornn will use his Q to poke, but it also opens the option of him using his E. If his E hits the terrain created by his Q, he’ll knock everything up in a circle surrounding it. Prioritize attacking him when he tries to buy items in lane because it’ll cancel it.

Pantheon is very similar to Renekton in lane. Watch his resource bar very closely and base trades off of this. His empowered Q does a lot and is also a ranged ability, so you'll see Pantheon try for this a lot into Gnar. Pantheon has to get fairly close to you in order to all in, so pay attention to your positioning. The most annoying thing about this matchup is his W. It's pretty much Braum's shield, so you can't proc your W on him if he's facing you. A good way around this is to curve Gnar's Q around him and proc it from behind since he can't turn around while using it. Pantheon's E is a gap closer, but not one you have to worry about much if you are positioning correctly. Once he hits level six, be careful with staying in lane for too long after he resets because it acts like a teleport early. Armor is your friend in this matchup, especially if he is building Lethality.

Stay away from terrain in this lane. Poppy’s E will stun if she pins you to terrain. This will lead to a devastating trade. Her Q is fairly easy to dodge. Poppy’s W will eat Gnar’s E, so be sure not to use your cooldown until the duration of her W is over. A good Poppy will be able to read when you are going to E.
Qiyana has a lot of burst early, so look to play safe. Armor is a must. Look to all-in her when she's low on mana.

Quinn's early game is pretty scary, but luckily Gnar has a pretty easy time poking her out of lane. Play this lane pretty safe early and poke with your Q. Avoid being hit by her E when you all in with your E as Mega Gnar. Her E will push you back midjump.

Renekton’s early game is extremely strong, so play very safe. Keep an eye on his Fury because his abilities gain extra effects and deal extra damage. Renekton’s E can only be cast twice if he hits something with the first cast of his E. Be very careful when approaching your minions because he will use them to get that extra cast. Gnar is able to kite Renekton very easily.

Rengar's passive makes him very mobile in top lane. This matchup can be very difficult if you don't play the waves correctly. Let his minions push to you and freeze the wave under your tower. This makes it so that Rengar can't abuse the bushes he has available to him in top lane. You can also shove the wave in, but this is rather difficult to do against Tiamat. You want to avoid bushes completely. Once Rengar hits level six, he gets a lot of roam pressure. Rengar's empowered W is a cleanse, so time your CC carefully. All inning with Mega Gnar is possible when he doesn't have his empowered W.

Riven has a lot of gap closers to get to you. Her E completely nulls out your Q damage. This lane is all about cooldowns. When Riven uses her abilities, take advantage of her. Be very careful of her R when low because her slash is an execute. Play this lane safe early and consider rushing Ninja Tabi.

Rumble’s Q is his main source of damage and Gnar outranges it. Avoid being hit by his E because it will let Rumble close the gap against Gnar to get his Q in range. His W is on a low cooldown and will always eat your Q damage. Once Rumble gets his R, be very careful. His R will slow you, deal a ton of damage, and ultimately lead to your death. Consider rushing MR in this matchup.

Ryze is a monster at clearing waves. This can make it difficult for Gnar to get lane priority. If Ryze is constantly pushing, ask your jungler for ganks. Be careful when he marks you with his E because it makes Ryze's abilities gain bonus effects. He is significantly weaker early, so look for plays then. Sadly, Ryze has the option to build Frozen Heart in this matchup. If he chooses to do this, know that you can't win trades.

The Sett matchup is very similar to the Darius matchup. Sett wins early until Gnar gets Phage and Ninja Tabi. After this, you have enough range and movement speed to kite Sett. Sett will use his Q to get closer to you and then he generally wants to use his E to pull you into a charged W. All you have to do to avoid this is use Gnar's E to escape Sett's E. Do not go for trades unless your E is up as Mini Gnar. If you are close enough to Mega Gnar transformation, you can go in for a trade, transform into Mega Gnar and all in. If Sett decides to use his R here, Gnar can ult Sett into a wall immediately after Sett finishes his ult animation. Once you get Frozen Mallet, if kited correctly, Sett will never be able to touch Gnar. Only go for smart trades/all-ins until this power spike.

Shen’s only way to close the gap against Gnar is his E and it has a long cooldown. He can null out some of your damage with his W, but it doesn’t last for very long. Abuse him when he uses both of these cooldowns.

Singed can be a very annoying lane for Gnar, but luckily he has a lot of counter play. Pay close attention to his mana early. His Q uses a lot of it and it’s his only way of clearing minions. Singed’s W will prevent Gnar from using his E. He also has to be very close to you in order to flip you with his E. The only way he can close the gap against Gnar is to use his R or if he takes Ghost., and that’s without Gnar having Frozen Mallet. Once you get your Frozen Mallet, kiting Singed is very easy. Some Singed players will proxy the first few waves. It’s very hard for Gnar to CS early under tower, so guard your jungler’s top side to prevent this from happening.

All of Sion’s abilities can easily be dodged. It also helps that he is a melee champion. A lot of the time, a Sion player will try to bush cheese early since his Q can be charged without giving vision, so play towards river at the beginning of lane phase. Always watch where your minions are because Sion can use his E on them to increase its range. Sion’s W will eat Gnar’s poke, but it’s on a long cooldown. When Sion is getting ganked when he has his R, he will consider using it to get away. If this is the case, flashing in front of him or using Gnar’s E to get in front of him will cause his R to collide with you, cancelling it.

Swain is very weak early and burns through mana rather quickly. Watch closely to his E usage. Punish him when he misses. If it hits, he has the opportunity to all-in you after level 6. His R takes a good bit to charge up early, but always respect the amount of healing he's able to drain from large minion waves.

Sylas' sustain makes it very difficult for Gnar to trade with him. He also has a gap closer and some range. Just Sylas being on the enemy team can hurt your team tremendously because he can steal your ult and use it whenever he wants without Gnar's Rage barrier. As you can imagine, a Gnar ultimate that isn't gated by Rage is devasting. Be very careful and be sure to let your team know when he grabs your R.

Teemo’s Q will blind, which is a nightmare for Gnar since he is an AA champion. Luckily, with Teemo’s Q being on cooldown, Gnar can abuse him. This is the key to winning lane. Stay out of Teemo’s range early to avoid being poked. Trade with Gnar’s Q. Since Teemo is squishy, you can easily push him out of lane or go for an all in with Mega Gnar. Once Gnar gets his R, all inning Teemo as Mega Gnar will almost always work out in your favor. Getting an early Oracle Lens will help you clear out his mushrooms.
Trundle is fairly easy to play against. He does have ways to close the gap against you with his pillar and his E. Avoid dueling him when he uses his R on you. Abuse him being melee.

Tryndamere can very easily be abused with Gnar because of him being a melee champion. Avoid going in for trades against Tryndamere when he has a lot of Fury because he gets increased crit chance and his Q will also heal him a lot. It takes Tryndamere has to AA to gain Fury, so abuse this. His E and W will help him close the gap against Gnar. All inning Tryndamere can be difficult when he has his R, so try and bait it out. Get Black Cleaver first and Frozen Mallet second. Prioritize Randuin's Omen as your third item to ease his crits. If Tryndamere is split pushing, consider picking up a Phantom Dancer to help with dueling him.

Urgot’s AA range is very short compared to Gnar’s. This lane is all about dodging Urgot’s Q. If he lands his Q, his W becomes a problem because it’ll lock on to Gnar through minions. Urgot’s E is his primary way of gap closing. When Gnar is low on health, avoid Urgot as much as possible because his R is an execute.
Viktor can be a tricky matchup because of his mobility and safety from his Q. He can also clear waves very fast once he upgrades his E. Poke with your Q and look for all-ins after level 6.

The counter to poke is sustain and sadly, Vladimir can do this incredibly well. To make matters worse, he is also a ranged champion. Vladimir’s W also makes him invulnerable. This makes all inning him as Mega Gnar almost impossible because he can W your CC. In order to win this matchup, you need to avoid his empowered Q and bait out his W before an all in. Poking him to death is impossible because of the amount of sustain he has.

Wukong has a very strong early game. Because Mini Gnar has very little health early, Wukong's burst can very easily kill you in a couple of his combos. Play safe early and poke with Q. Once you get armor, look for trades/all-ins.

Yasuo is an absolute nightmare for Gnar. His E can be used indefinitely as long as he has minions to use it on. Because of this, Gnar’s only option to stay at a range is to step far from his own minion wave. The best time to trade with Yasuo is when he has no minions to E through. Watch carefully for when Yasuo has his tornado. Yasuo’s W will eat Gnar’s Q and put it on the full cooldown. It’ll also stop Mega Gnar’s Q from travelling.

Yorick’s only way to trade with you is if he lands his E. His E will slow and mark you, causing his Mist Walkers to jump to you. You absolutely have to dodge this ability. Yorick can raise his Mist Walkers if three or more graves are created. Watch very carefully for this since this is most likely when Yorick will try to trade with you. Save your E for when Yorick hits his E or casts his W. Avoid all inning him when his Maiden is attacking you because Yorick will extra damage to you.

You will find Anivia in the Mid lane the majority of the time, but you might get the extremely rare Anivia player that will counter pick your Gragas and follow you to whichever lane you go. You can move around her terrain with E but a good Anivia can cancel your E with her Wall if you try to engage. She out ranges you, out waveclears, and can put on some serious damage if she knows what shes doing. A very good Anivia makes for a very hard lane.

Cho'gath can match your early Lane sustain. The difference is he can also out-sustain your mana pool early on. A good Cho'gath wont give you much breathing room. If he comes back with some MR then you wont actually have any kill potential on them unless they horribly misplay. If you're the only AP on your team a Cho'gath might get greedy and build Armor first, if this is the case you should be able to sneak a kill in before he becomes too tanky. Basically extremely Tanky and hard to kill at all stages of the game. Play to scale and target the carries in fights.

Rare Top/Mid pick, most common in Jungle. She can brawl in melee range better than you especially with Conqueror. You will need to take short trades and disengage. Be careful of her dash reset because she can leap back on to you if you try to E her back. Short trades and Q poke will help you come out on top of this match up. Never take extended fights as she will always win.

Dr. Mundo has a lot of regeneration and is very hard to kill especially without Grevious Wounds. What makes Gragas Top really good is his abilities to disrupt and disengage at will. Dr. Mundo can ignore your CC with his passive, and if he builds tenacity can just run you down with cleavers. Hard to kill, hard to get away from.

110% Mind game match up. A good, patient, and smart Fiora is a nightmare to deal with. This matchup becomes even more difficult if she takes Tenacity runes and Merc treads. That being said.. If she doesn't take Tenacity, and just throws out her W unga bunga, then she will be an extremely easy match up. Play around her W, if you stun yourself she can all-in 100-0 you.

Another Ranged match up where the higher the skill the harder it gets. You don't have any effective way to deal with turrets early on so you will just have to sit under your tower avoiding poke and CSing as much as possible. Once you complete Lost Chapter you can start looking for Q poke and if they get too cocky you can ult them into your turret for a free lead.

A rare pick Top, so you would be more likely to come across Olaf in the jungle. Olaf can stick to you with Q and can sustain quite heavily with his W. His R makes it so you can't E or R him away, so your best bet is to go for a full combo to proc Phase Rush, and run away while avoiding his Q. After using his R he becomes a lot easier to deal with.

Until they decide to tone down Sett's obnoxious strength he will be my GO-TO ban. This match up gets significantly easier the less experienced and lower rank the Sett is, but a good Sett is just going to stack Tenacity and E you on cooldown to choke you out of lane. It's very hard to bully Sett out of lane because his Passive HP regen makes it so he will never be in Lethal.

Same deal as Mundo, extremely hard to kill and is able to stick to you easily with tenacity. You will basically need to outfarm and outscale. A poor Tahm Kench will let you combo endlessly, if this happens you might be able to squeeze a kill. You'll need to stay out of melee range at all costs.

There have been a couple of Masters+ Teemos that could give me a run for my money. If played correctly this matchup should come to a stalemate, you might get harassed off of a CS lead. Other than that, if they misposition and suck, it's a very easy lane.

A good Vayne should never get hit by your abilities. This is another lane where you will need to fight carefully for your CS and wait for ganks. If the Vayne has poor positioning this match up becomes exponentially easier.

Another Range match up that can match your sustain. You will have to play to CS before your first back because if you decide to blow your Mana pool Vladimir can look for an All-in Level 6. The only way you win this is if you're able to continuously poke, and they grief their pool. Getting wounds will help deter Vlad from looking to trade with you.

Yone when stacking Tenacity runes can be really hard to shake off. His E counters your kit in a way where if you look to pick him with R he can use E to dodge, and then snap back. E is the most important cooldown to play around. Try to keep him at a distance if he is trying to chase you down.

Definitely a skill and knowledge match up, but the better the Yorick the harder it gets. The most important thing you need to keep in mind is that you can't get caged, because if you do it's an easy 100-0 for the Yorick. You can sometimes E out of a sticky situations but his Ghouls make it insanely hard to get an E off and they make it hard to move around in general. If Yorick doesn't buy MR or Tenacity then he can be very easy to kill if he wastes his abilities.

Another hard but rare Top lane pick. Again you will more commonly run into this match up in the jungle. Xin stacking Tenacity will be incredibly hard to shake off, but if the Xin Zhao neglects taking any Tenacity, you should be able to disengage and keep him neutralized just fine. Obviously, don't take an extended fight.

I personally have quite a bit of mental block against Aatrox in general, but I find this is a difficult lane regardless. This is a match up where I would highly recommend picking up an early Oblivion Orb after Lost Chapter. If he chains you then E out, and avoid his Empowered Q hitboxes at all costs. It's hard for you to kill each other but he will always win extended fights.

I would put Akali lower but I don't feel like I've gone against a really solid Akali player. This lane is fairly easy as you can negate a lot of her early harass with Passive/W spam. If she lands E on to you she can't reliably engage without getting chunked by your E - Combo on her E activation. When she shrouds look to kite out. Her R can do some serious damage if you aren't careful. Fight only on your terms.

A hand full of Gragas players I've talked to feel like Camille is a nightmare to play against. While a good Camille that stacks tenacity can be extremely difficult to play against, I would say Camille needs to play pretty flawlessly to win (as long as you aren't griefing). W start and passive healing will negate her W harass. Kite out her AA Q and disengage her E with your E. If you look to all-in you need to keep in mind her passive shield cooldown and you also need to keep in mind that she can R to dodge any of your abilities.

Annoying range match up but not as bad as Teemo. Preserve your mana pool early and stay healthy with Passive/W healing. Once you get a Lost Chapter and points in Q you can look to start trading back. Always stay far away from Mega Gnar. If you managed to poke Gnar enough when he's about to leave Mega Gnar you can look to all-in.

Pretty rare lane but can be difficult depending on the skill of the player. Graves has no real kill threat on you unless you let him free hit AA you. The best time to trade with Graves is when he dashes in. Use you combo and chunk him, then look for an all-in if he gets too low and blows his E.

I would have this at max difficulty but against Irelia needs to play perfect in order to squeeze kills out of you. Be mindful of the minion wave and disengage with E Combo when she dashes on to you. This match up is heavily reliant on wave management. If she can freeze infront of her tower she can all-in 100-0 with just a Vamp Sceptre. If this ends up being the case you can Combo-Phase Rush out and R her away if needed. This will break her freeze and leave her R on a longer cooldown than yours. This is about the only window you get to kill her unless she sucks.

If you're good at avoiding his Q then this is a fairly easy range match up. Preserve mana and sustain through your Passive/W. Once you get your Lost Chapter you can look to throw out a lot of poke. Jayce should never be able to Melee form combo you because you can CANCEL his Q with your E and full combo him instead.

Mostly just an extremely annoying lane. You should be able to sustain through her early poke and CS. I wouldn't try fighting her because her permanent 600MS makes her pretty hard to hit. She can be cheesed infront of your tower if she gets too cocky, and it becomes easier once you've completed Everfrost.

As far as threat goes Nasus really has no kill potential on you. If Nasus greeds for too much CS you can start spamming W AA's on him in the early levels. After about his 2nd back he should be strong enough to fight back and if you aren't careful he can wither you and run you down. Play for early roams and picks around the map. Nasus will outscale you if the player is good and doesn't let you kill him.

I was debating leaving Nocturne in because his meta in lane was fairly short lived this season. That being said he has great early sustain through his passive and can poke you and waveclear well with Q. A good Nocturne will hold his W until he sees you try to E them. A good way to keep yourself from getting Spellshielded is to walk close to him and see if he panic spellshields. If not he wont have time to react to a melee range E. If he does panic spellshield keep in mind that he might do it again and wait out the shield. Use your Phase Rush to break his E tether.

Considered a counter to Gragas because her W can block your E. This is kind of the same deal as Nocturne where if you're in melee range she shouldn't be able to react to your E. Play for CS early on and look to outshine in teamfights. You'll be able to kill her after Everfrost if she neglects buying any MR.

For the most part a pretty afk farm lane. After Mythic you should be able to beat Ryze, but after about Level 11 his damage will scale to threatening levels. Keep your trades short and get the most out of your Phase Rush. If they're aggressive in early laning phase just sustain through your Passive/W spam.

Sylas wins every extended trade you take so you need to keep your Combos and movement quick. Early Oblivion Orb is NEEDED if you're looking for kills. You lose until you get Lost Chapter. Once you have Lost Chapter you'll be able to sustain and farm safely, or play aggressive if you think you can kill him.

Viego Top is becoming a lot more rare recently. His sustain on minions isn't as obnoxious as it was on release but I would still consider buying an Oblivion Orb early on. You'll be able to sustain through his Q poke early with your Passive/W. Never look for an extended trade/fight with Viego because you will lose 100% of the time. Be careful when you go for an all-in because he can use his R to cancel the CC from either your E or R.

WW Top is usually taken with Barrier. Early on you obviously can't trade with him so you'll have to look for as much CS as you can and sustain through Passive/W. I would say this match up is heavily skill based once you've completed Lost Chapter and picked up Oblivion Orb. You will need to play around his Q CC negation and E Damage Reduction. After he takes some poke and it looks like you might have an opening keep spamming Q on him before he tries to heal off the wave, and try to bait his E with a Phase Rush combo, and All in. This is best played close to your tower, because if the lane extends he can chase you down fairly easily.

I actually haven't played this match up in about 2 years. Darius for the longest time has been my perma-ban as I like to keep the option for picking Sion open. Recently I've been switching to Tahm/Sett bans in Masters+ because Darius' pickrate has fallen off over the years and Sett/Tahm lanes are extremely toxic and unplayable. I'll revisit this after I've played this match up.

Gangplank before Laning nerfs was pretty easy to sustain through. Every time he goes for Q you can just W with your passive up and take virtually no damage. Early CS should be easy and once you get Lost Chapter he should be fairly easy to poke down and kill. When you do look for a kill make sure to respect his W heal. Becomes even easier if you can break barrels, and as an Ex-GP OTP, this lane is a joke.

The only thing you need to look out for in this lane is if Garen can get on to you and Spin while your E is down. CSing early should be a breeze and once you get Lost Chapter throwing combos at Garen will chunk him pretty hard. I've fallen asleep and gotten cheesed by Garen players who take Ignite and Nuke me with their ult, but you will completely take over the Mid-game after your Mythic.

Gwen is only difficult if you tank every single Q-E she throws out and let her AA you to death. Passive/W spam early on will help you deal with her harass and keep you healthy. If she dashes into you without minions to block you can win very short trades with a simple E-W. Before you try using your R on her you'll need to make sure she used her W. If at any point she uses her R you need to proc Phase Rush as fast as possible and GTFO. Her R slows for a lot and deals MASSIVE damage.

W Level 1 will negate her Q Level 1. Get lots of CS and if she positions poorly you can look for quick E-W trades. You need to avoid her E at all costs. If you let her hit E a lot this match up will become much harder. 100% of Illaoi's get too cocky and start trying to trade under your tower. Throw a Q on her for the slow and then R her back towards you under the tower (if you can clear the minions with this it is a guaranteed kill). A strong Illaoi player can avoid this with her R CC negation, but once this happens shes open to getting ganked, and your R will be on a shorter CD.

Jax never has a reliable way to get on to you unless you get in range of him to E and walk at you. Level 2 Jax players get overly aggressive and just Spam Q-E. What you need to do is E every time he Q's on to you, and then WAIT for your E cooldown. Jax's Q has a short CD so he has small 3-4 second openings to jump on you after failing the first time. Keep this in mind and this should be a neutral lane until you get Lost Chapter and can start poking with Q.

Kayle poses no threat early on. It's a very neutral lane until you reach Lost Chapter. You can use your early game spike to look to punish her for CSing and even get a kill if she greeds too much. If they game goes on too long she will eventually outscale and become a monster, but if you can R her into your team she'll be very easy to kill.

Kennen's early harass can be dealt with pretty easily with your Passive/W spam. It's important to not give him free Electrocute procs. After Lost Chapter you should be able to bully Kennen away from you with Q poke. If he mispositions you might even be able to get a combo or too off. Remember that Kennen can dodge your E with his E movement speed, and if you miss your E you are most certainly going to die to his R. If he pops his R during one of your combos use Phase Rush to run away. In teamfights you can use your R to knock him away if he tries to engage onto your team.

The difficulty obviously rises the better the Kled is, but I almost always find this lane extremely free. Early levels Kled will spam Q for harass which is easy to dodge, and can be sustained back up through W. After Level 3 every single Kled player will do the exact same thing; they wait for their W to be available, and blow their entire load on you when you go to last hit. This is very easily disengaged from by using E. Dump some combo's on him once you get mana sustain and he should be an easy kill. Be careful using your combo when he dismounts so you don't lose damage, and make sure you can kill him before he remounts.

Lee Sin top has become a little bit more tame after some of the nerfs. Early on you're just looking for CS and sustain, you can do simple W-E trades if you find he wants to walk up for hugs all the time. I recommend Oblivion Orb before finishing Everfrost so that you actually have kill potential on him.

3000+ games of Sion hasn't taught me very much about playing against him. In this match up I usually rush Liandry's and play to bully him off as much CS as I can. Eventually Sion will reach a point where you wont be able to kill him alone, so if he's split heavy you will need to call for help. That being said you have plenty of ways to disrupt him in a teamfight and you can maneuver around better than him.

This lane is 100% free unless Urgot permanently holds his E for your E. Sustain his early poke through Passive/W and once you get Lost Chapter you should be able to poke him into Lethal range. The most important thing in this match up is to play around his E, if he lands it he will shred your entire health bar.

Malphite should be absolutely 0 threat. Passive/W sustain will negate his early Q poke and he will run out of mana pretty fast. You can look to take an aggressive position in the minion wave and trade with your W-E whenever its available. Malphite can avoid being Kegged by Ulting away, but his ult is a lot more important in a teamfight than yours.

Maokai Top is pretty much going extinct. Look to out CS early and take short W-E trades if he tries to get on you. You'll have a hard time killing him without Oblivion Orb but he should also never be able to kill you. CS and outscale.

Level 1 your W completely negates his Q poke. If he pulls you in, W and E to disengage. Once you build Lost Chapter you can start going for fast combos if he positions poorly. Save your R for his R as it will help you create space and stay alive. Once he wastes ult hes an easy gank and free kill.

Passive/W sustain negates his Q Level 1. The best tip I have against Ornn is to dodge the last tick of his W so he can't apply brittle and get %HP damage and knock back off of auto attacking you. You can use your E to cancel his E so that he can't knock you up. You also have the option of CCing him with E or R when he goes to R2. Respect a good Ornn who uses W to cancel your CC. Don't go for any fancy R combo's if his W is available.

Play back a little bit early and sustain with Passive/W. You can cancel his W with your E if you time it correctly. After you get Lost Chapter this lane basically becomes free. The only thing that will lose you this lane is if you blow an entire combo on his E. Make sure you communicate when he leaves lane as he can R around the map.

A great Quinn can be a nightmare to deal with, but you have lots of tools to deal with her. Passive/W for early sustain. You can cancel her E with your E if timed correctly. Most Quinns struggle against well placed Q's so after you've landed a couple of barrels you can use the slow to R her for an easy kill. Obviously respect Quinns with great spacing.

Another early bully that can be survived through your Passive/W sustain. Use your E to disengage whenever he looks to trade. Once you get Lost Chapter you can start looking to throw Q's and combos at him. His Lethal range is very low HP as he can regain HP with R+Q very fast, but more Renektons will be greedy and try to outplay you. Only go for a kill if you can burst through his R&Q heal.

Sit back Level 1 and let him do whatever he wants. Once you hit level 2 you can E him if he tries to leap on you. Make sure you stay far away from bushes when your E is on cooldown. Eventually most Rengars will just stop trying to engage on you and start clearing and roaming, so make sure you communicate with pings whenever Rengar leaves lane. Pick a Seeker's if you're struggling.

Another champion that can do whatever she wants level 1. Wait for level 2 and use your E to disengage when she tries to dash on you. You can CANCEL her Q3 during her flip with E to avoid the knockup and damage. Very easy unless she gets a kill. Respect her when she gets Merc Treads and build Oblivion Orb early on as needed.

I've only played this lane a handful of times but you can usually just sustain up early and put on pressure once you get Lost Chapter. You need to respect his heat because his damage will significantly increase if he uses a full combo and overheats.

I have never struggled with this lane. You need to respect his E-Q all-in but you can usually disengage with a full combo and sustain back up. Every trade he takes he will end up slowly losing because you can use your Passive to heal back up. Play around his E cooldown and you will be all over him.

If the Singed player is good he can buffer his fling and flip you whenever you go to E him. Close range your E is incredibly hard to react to so keep him poked with Q's and use Phase Rush to full combo and back off so he doesn't have the chance to fling. Obviously don't chase Singed and wait for him to misposition before going for anything crazy.

Should be fairly free unless they're a god at trundle. He isn't really worth trading with so just CS until you get Lost Chapter and poke him with Q's. You can outrun his pillar slow with Phase Rush if you combo him, but if you're using E to run away then a good Trundle will pillar you and kill you if you're too far extended from your tower.

Respect his level 1 RNG crit all-in and you basically win the lane for free. After level 2 you can use E whenever he tries to E on to you, and if he hits his slow you can full combo to Phase Rush out. If Tryndamere tries to dive you with ult make sure you have your tools available to kite him out.

I'm rarely seeing this match up as of Patch 11.18 but you never want him to get a W2 off on you. Eating his full combo will do a lot of damage to you so play around his Q engage. Once you have Lost Chapter you can poke him with Q and combo him at will. Never get too low from trades as he can dive you with R and his jungler with very little counterplay.

This lane is FREE. A lot of Wukong players are blindly aggressive for no reason and end up getting chunked every time they try to E on to you. Prepare to E his E and combo him. Eventually they'll either get frustrated and fold or back off and let you do whatever you want with the wave. A good Wukong builds Merc Treads and pokes with Q. You want to force a stalemate by keeping your E available only for when he jumps on you. Otherwise he can clone your E or just tank your E and THEN jump on you. VERY hard to deal with after he gets a kill or 2.

Can be very annoying levels 1-2 with Q spam and E dash spam. Remember to hold your E for whenever he tries to dash onto you and you can force a stalemate. Once you get Lost Chapter you can harass him with Q's. NEVER use your R unless he just recently used wind wall. Play away a bit from your minion wave so that if he wants to all-in you he can't use your wave to maneuver around. You can usually disengage his all-in and sustain back up unless he let yourself get in lethal range. If he doesn't build MR then he will get nuked after you finish your first item.

Zac top is not common but very easy to deal with. Usually in this lane you can farm to Lost Chapter for free and start pumping Q's into him. Your E can cancel his E while he is airborne. You can also R his E channel or while he is airborne for a flashy catch. I recommend Oblivion Orb directly after Everfrost/Liandry's so that he can't sustain with his blobs. When he is in his passive drop a Q and let it charge and then W when they're all clumped to easily deal with his tiny blobs.

Accelerate ahead with your superior farming and look to countergank. You outscale him hard same as reksai. and your E negates their burst potential if you're even

| Whoever gets ahead wins this matchup to be honest. You can dash his W and be pretty ok. The issue is, even if he is behind. If you facecheck him into a W he will oneshot you if he has BORK. Even if he doesn't and has sunderer he kills you. | An argument can be made to put him on major since he can chase you down and beat you in all out 1v1. | If you pilot graves well and be aware it's not too bad

Allowing him to both tank a lot of damage, deal a lot of damage CC and provide zone control. | However this doesn't mean he is good into graves it just means he is overpowered. Graves can easily kite him and hit him with some serious damage. He has no real kill pressure on you either unless you eat saplings. | He should be ranked higher but he will be nerfed and honestly. The champs overpowered the actual matchup into graves is not favourable but he will win 55% of the time simply because his items/abilities are broken in a team game/damage sense.

| 50/50. She prevents you from dashing. Deals magic damage which you are weak to. On the flipside you kill her if you catch her out of position and if you're fed she does nothing to you (if you have MR). | Even from behind you can kill her too. | It's imperative you do not dash into her E. or be thrown into it through her E W combo. Failure to do this makes this matchup a nightmare.

| Sejuani gets outscaled. You can't kill her early or at any stage of the game until you have penetration (BC/Serylda) She's far too tanky and the onslaught of slows CC and dashes makes her a nightmare for you to chase. | You do outscale her but be advised, if she accelerates her team early she can transition into the supportive tank role for her DPS in which circumstance you HARD lose the game. | The trick is to prevent sejuani from having a backline to play with. Without a strong backline sejuani is just a general without an army
