If you're facing Aphelios in the early game, take advantage of his weaker state and punish him accordingly. It will prevent him from becoming a significant threat as the game progresses. To keep him under control, try to poke at him consistently. However, be cautious if he has his chakram weapon, as he can dish out damage quickly, making it difficult to match him. It's best not to engage him alone in this situation.

Winning this matchup is simple, but don't underestimate her w and r since they can be the death of you. Also, be mindful of your positioning when fighting Ashe to avoid getting slowed down by her auto attacks.
Caitlyn is more of a skill matchup for Miss Fortune, so as long as you avoid her traps and catch her when she uses q. Apart from this, you should be fine.

Corki has solid damage from his hextech munitions (passive), phosphorus bomb and missile barrage, so adequate spacing and positioning will be necessary. One thing to note when dueling him, his gatling gun shreds your overall resistance to physical and magical attacks, which could turn the tables in his favor depending on how long you fight him. Corki can get within striking distance of you, knocking you aside with valkyrie. Therefore, disengaging sooner is best to avoid being run down if you are in low health. Good positioning is critical in this matchup.

What can I say but don't take extended fights, and you only win all-ins against him with some help. Instead, poke him often with your skills while watching for his "stand aside" ability, and make sure not to take too many empowered axes from him.
Another skill matchup, so the only thing you need to do is watch out for his w + q combo and make sure he uses e and or his flash before engaging with him.

The big thing you need to be aware of in this matchup is to avoid fighting him when he has his fourth shot since it does more damage based on your missing health. Instead, attack him only when he's out of bullets and is reloading.

Your objective in this matchup is to punish Jinx whenever she approaches to hit minions, as her range is limited early on with pow-pow (minigun), making her vulnerable to your double-up bounces. However, if you see her using fishbones when you walk up to punish her, retreat and regroup. Be cautious when she places flame chompers, as getting trapped could lead to sudden death. Another concern in this matchup (after level 9) is that her attack range is higher than Miss Fortune's while she is using fishbones (rocket launcher). Therefore, it is harder to approach Jinx unless you can close the gap.

Kai'Sa's burst and her ability to break vision with her evolved supercharge separate you from winning all the trades and fights. Avoid taking too much damage from her passive, and you'll be better off in this matchup.

This matchup is skill-reliant because of the mobility in her passive. The abilities you need to focus on are her rend & ultimate, making this matchup harder during extended fights. Watch your health bar around Kalista and coordinate with your team to take her down.
Kog'Maw is easy to take down, so just don't let him kill you too much. The big thing to do is poke him down in the lane often before level 6.

This matchup isn't hard, but bait his dash out before channelling your ultimate. Make sure to poke him often using make it rain for good damage, and avoid taking long trades with Lucian unless you get the upper hand.

Watch out for Nilah's jubilant veil (w), which dodges basic attacks and reduces magic damage & apotheosis (r) that interrupts your bullet times channel and pulls you close. Preventing her from last hitting minions denies the bonus gold and experience from her passive. A tough matchup for you if you make too many mistakes.

She is very mobile with wild rush (resets on takedown), alongside her blade whirl that can block double up, ultimate and your auto attacks. Both of these abilities help with stacking her passive. Fighting Samira is hard because she has safe laning with her flair ability and gets lifesteal early on to survive our poke damage. Make sure to have healing reduction available to deal with her effectively.

It's important to note that while Miss Fortune has higher base damage in the game's early stages, Senna has greater scaling potential. When facing Senna, it's crucial to avoid getting hit by her abilities, such as her W, "Last Embrace," and her Q, "Piercing Darkness," which can slow you down. Additionally, Piercing Darkness can heal Senna, while her ultimate ability, "Dawning Shadow," can provide her with a shield. Therefore, keeping an eye on her positioning and coordinating with your team before engaging her is advisable.

The easiest way to beat Sivir in fights is to avoid taking too much damage from her q poke and be mindful of her positioning and her itemization. Apart from that, she's easy for you to deal with in the lane.

Defeating Smolder requires careful positioning and a favorable support matchup while in the lane. Disrupting his farming with your support can make it easier to handle him. Keep in mind that he scales well into the late game, so it's important to exercise caution when engaging in fights.

This champion out-scales you if she gets ahead. Her all-in potential is very potent, so avoid being shoved too far. It's best to play safe and get your support to bait out her skills, thus giving you a window to pounce on her after she is on cooldown.

This matchup is straightforward, dodge his w ability to avoid being affected by the poison and take a hit from his contaminate ability. Be sure to watch out if he goes invisible too as he may bait you into an extended trade that might not be favourable.
He outranges you massively in the lane and has a larger poke radius with his q, e and r. Due to this range difference you could get poked out and set behind.

Vayne is only a threat unless she picks up a few early takedowns. Vayne's condemn ability is also something to watch out for since it will cancel your ultimate and pin you into a wall or structure, so do your best to position yourself safely when attacking her. She scales well in long games, so you should keep an eye on her.

Just keep track of her movements and feather placements to avoid getting rooted by her ultimate and have it lead to you potentially dying. Xayah's ultimate can dodge our abilities (becoming untargetable), so try to bait her ultimate before you engage for the best results.

Dealing with Zeri is straightforward during the lane phase. She can slow us down with her w and gains movement speed as she attacks with her ultimate. All you need to do is poke her down at every turn and do your best to avoid her empowered w (guaranteed crit) that anchors off walls and structures.

While your E is great to deny her E, you need to time it well or she will simply break it before charming you. Thanks to her ult and the movement speed boost on her W, she can also dodge your Q and get out of your R with ease. Consider buying an early Verdant Barrier in lane if you struggle.
She can also avoid your Q and R rather easily. Don't waste your Q or she will run you down. Hold it until you need it and make it count.
Akshan can be a bit rough, depending on how good he is. You can never really trade with him, and if you miss Q, you will be in trouble. Buy control wards for prepare for his botlane roams.

She outranges and outdamages you at any point in the game. When you ult, she will either just turn and burst you down or put distance between you and herself with her W. Try to coordinate ganks with your jungler early on. Abuse her weak pre-6 by shoving her under tower and invading the enemy jungler together with your jungler.

The annoying part about Annie is that you cannot really react to her R-stun, so you need to respect it a lot. Outside of that, the matchup is fine. She can't really get away from you once you ult. Time your E well to prevent her from breaking the shield before stunning. If she gets an early kill, consider buying an early Verdant Barrier in lane to reduce her further kill pressure. Be aware that Tibbers can block your Q.

In lane against him you are more than fine, so he's gonna do what he does and shove the wave and then run off and gank your botlane. Run TP so you can follow and countergank him. Always have a Control Ward in the river and spam-ping your botlane QUICKLY when he starts flying off.

You also cannot really stop him from scaling through the roof. Try to spellshielding his R when he tries to insec you to leave him in an awkward spot. Be very wary of him trying to R you into his jungler.
His poke is very annoying, but his lack of mobility also makes him vulnerable to your kit. Make sure not to waste your E on poke unless you're absolutely sure you won't need it otherwise.

Easy matchup if she's bad, but very bad if she's good. Her constant DPS is just too much for you and your high cooldowns on Q and E. The second you miss your Q, she can just run you down. Try to predict her R because otherwise she will simply break your shield before using it. Call your jungler for help as soon as she starts to play aggressive and hope that she overextends. Be aware of her 1v2 potential at lvl 6 and afterwards though.
Very easy matchup for obvious reasons. He's very straightforward and cannot really play around your Q and E.

Just like you, he has rather high mana costs and cooldowns. If he ever uses his W for no reason during the laning phase, run him down with ult. Try to coordinate with your jungler to abuse him early and punish him for picking Corki outside of proplay. He will, however, outscale you, so be aware that you're on a timer.
Don't waste your Q or she might run you down and force you to ult. Try to spellshield her ult. If you fail to do so, start ulting yourself and chain it with your Q if she stays inside it.

His rather high cooldowns at the start of the game make him an easy lane opponent for you. Spellshield his stun and save your Q for when he uses E on you during the early levels. Try to match his push by putting your W down often because Morgana sucks at lasthitting under tower. In teamfights, shield whoever he is trying to burst and then Q him before he can ult out so your team can burst him down.

Sololane Ezreal can be very annoying for you. Not only can he kite you rather easily, he can also run you down with Qs and autoattacks after dodging your Q. Keep in mind that his E cooldown is very high early on. Turn on him if he ever uses it offensively. If he does it a lot, let your jungler iknow.

While she is usually not played as a midlaner, I'm including her here because she is a pretty bad match-up for Morgana. She will easily outdamage you and just run you down at any point in the game, she can dodge most of your Qs and you can never ult when near her because it's extremely easy for her to time her parry for the second instance of your ult.

He has plenty of ways to outplay you and dodge everything you do and he can simply oneshot you at level 6. This can be helped by going Spellbook and cycling through defensive summoner spells. If he ever loses interest in you and switches his attention to your botlane, keep a Control Ward in the river at all times and spam-ping your botlane every time he roams. Buying an early Verdant Barrier can significantly reduce his kill pressure on you.

Your spellshield counters his entire kit pretty hard. He is also an easy Q target because of how telegraphed his dash is. He will try to push you in and roam. Warn your botlane in advance. Try to be wherever he tries to go and countergank him since your Q and E shut him down rather hard.
He outdamages you and can remove your Q/R with his W. He will simply run you down. Try to coordinate with your jungler and shut him down during his W cooldown.

Your W is great for clearing turrets and your E is great for blocking his stun. Time your E well so he doesn't break it before his stun. The worst that can happen to you in this matchup is that he forces you to lasthit under tower.

You usually don't have enough damage to 1v1 her even if you otherwise outplay her, but you can heavily shut her down in teamfights. Be patient with your Q. Be aware that she can get out of your R if there's targets for her to Q on. Just try to survive lane.
He hurts. Try to not miss your Q (duh). If you do, he will run you down. Play safe while it is on cooldown. Thankfully, nobody plays this guy. Buy an early Seeker's Armguard if necessary.
Pretty much impossible for you to actually kill him, so he will simply outscale you for free. Your only chance here is to coordinate with your jungler and try to put him behind early.
Her mobility and DPS is nhard for you to deal with if she's good. Call your jungler for help. Keep a control ward in the river and spam-ping your sidelanes when she roams.

Kayle is rather vulnerable due to your Qs due to her lack of mobility, however, there comes a point in every game against her where she just snowballs/scales away from you and you can no longer go near her without being torn to pieces before your R even goes off. Abuse her lack of mobility and early game power by calling your jungler to camp her and never let her get into the game.

Annoying, but her high cooldowns make this match-up bearable. Try to not be too predictable with your Qs. Keep shoving the wave and ask her in all-chat if she's having fun lasthitting under tower. In teamfights, try to spot her early and babysit your ADC. If you hit a Q on her, your team can almost certainly kill her instantly. Get an early Verdant Barrier to reduce her kill pressure if necessary.

She has very high cooldowns, her kit is rather predictable and doesn't work well against yours. You can deny her cc pretty hard if you time your spellshield correctly. Your Q prevents her from reactivating her E.
His high constant damage output and high mobility make him a dangerous lane opponent. Consider buying an early Seeker's Armguard. Don't be predictable with your Q, you need to hit it.

You can easily spellshield her Q and she also has no mobility to dodge your Q or get out of your R. Her range and poke in lane can be annoying, consider buying boots very early to make dodging her poke easier.

A single tick from your W is enough to remove his passive. Keep that in mind when trying to cc him. Try to match his push with your W so you don't have to lasthit under tower (you both suck at doing that early on). His voidlings can be annoying since they can block your Q, and you might not be able to spellshield his ult since you have to predict it and can't simply react to it. Consider buying a QSS is he keeps ulting you every fight.
Who plays Morgana Midlane?

Her poke is annoying in the first few levels, but after that, you win hard. Her kit is super straight forward. Spellshield her E. If you don't react in time or don't have it ready, simply wait for her to ult and then spellshield that. Whenever she ults is also a good opportunity for you to land your Q since she has to stay still for a moment.
Usually she's very hard for similar reasons as Viktor or Cassio, but luckily she's so bad in the current meta that it's not as bad right now.
Very annoying early due to his high damage output. Be aware that he might just start perma-roaming bot if he cannot kill you past 6. Buy an early Seeker's Armguard if necessary.

He doesn't have much kill potential on you if you don't mess up your spellshield. You can kill him rather easily while his E is on cooldown. He will most likely just leave you alone and roam botlane over and over again, keep a Control Ward in the river at all times. Buy an early Seeker's Armguard if necessary.

While you can technically spellshield her stuns easily, her low cooldowns, good waveclear and high mobility make her very difficult to deal with. Keep a Control Ward on the map at all times to reduce her roam potential. Buy an early Seeker's Armguard if necessary.

His empowered W breaks shields (yes, even magic damage shields) BEFORE it applies the stun, making it impossible to spellshield. Buy an early Seeker's Armguard, respect his strong early game a lot and wait for him to fall off. Give up farm if necessary.

He outdamages you and you cannot really kill him in a 1v1 at any point, but he is also a very easy Q target since he literally just runs at you. Try to match his push so you don't have to lasthit under tower.

Ryze's laning phase is pretty bad, he will struggle mana a lot, and he also cannot really dodge your Q. However, he will outscale you significantly, so try to not drag the game out too much. Abuse his weak laning phase with your jungler and then help them take dragons and heralds to accelerate the game.

Seraphine's laning phase is very weak. A bit like Morgana, except her waveclear is worse. However, just like you, she will start shining in skirmishes and teamfights. Coordinate ganks with your jungler to abuse her lack of mobility.

His E is pretty easy to spellshield with how telegraphed it is. If he's close enough, he might try to Q you right before his E hits you to break your spellshield, be aware of that and time it well. In teamfights, zone him and prevent him from getting good value out of his ultimate with your Q and R.

Running exhaust is an option here to shut him down throughout the game. Play around his E cooldown and try to spellshield it. He gets amazing value out of stealing your ult. Get an early Oblivion Orb.

Make sure to time your spellshield very well so that she doesn't break it before attempting to stun you. If you fail at doing so, she can oneshot you. Get early boots to make dodging her skillshots easier. Most junglers can easily gank and kill her if you spellshield he E onto your jungler. Get an early Verdant Barrier.
He can't really ever kill you unless you mess up hard, but what he can do is roam and snowball. So keep a ward in the river at all times and ping early.

Trist mid can be a pain in the ass. If you ever waste your Q, she will all-in you and at least chunk you out of lane heavily. You also cannot really prevent her from constantly shoving and taking some platings. Coordinate ganks with your jungler.

His kit is very straight forward and spellshielding his gold card in clutch situations should not be a problem. However, be aware that his W has a much lower cooldown than your E. He will try to bully you whenever your E is down. Try to keep the wave pushed and ward the places he usually ults from. Be aware that his ult has a casttime of 1.5 seconds and your Q has a very slow travel time, so you need to be very quick if you want to cancel his ult with Q.
His kit is very straight forward and his cage is super easy to spellshield. He is also an easy Q target. Be aware of his burst damage with ult though.

Vel'Koz outranges and outdamages you by a lot. NEVER waste your E on his Q and W poke when he has E and R ready, try to dodge it instead. Buy early boots to make dodging easier. You can catch him offguard and Q him while he's ulting someone else.

Viktor usually wins lane vs Morgana and also outscales her hard. In teamfights, he can also nuke you as soon as you start to R. Try to abuse his lack of mobility and get your jungler to gank him a lot early.

Vladimir is generally not a huge problem for you in lane, however, he will outscale you and there's not a whole lot you can do about it. Try to abuse his high W cooldown with your jungler and then take objectives together to close out the game quickly. Buy an early Oblivion Orb.

His poke is very annoying to deal with, but once you're close to him, he's in trouble. He's very squishy and has no ways of dodging your Q or getting out of your ult. Time your E well to spellshield his stun when running him down. Buy early boots to make dodging easier.

The Yasuo matchup is surprisingly easy. He has no magic damage to break your shield and he can only get out of your R if there's targets to dash on nearby. Don't try to Q him if his Windwall is ready, instead, start the fight with ult, wait for the ult to stun him, then melee range Q him. Exhaust makes this matchup a lot easier. In teamfights, prevent him from doing anything with your E. Shut him down with Q and R as soon as he goes in. His best bet here is to sidelane instead because you make teamfights too difficult for him.

He is very mobile and has a lot of consistent DPS. Your best bet is to team up on him with multiple people and "camp" his E shadow in fights for an easy Q or R as soon as he goes back. If he tries to fight you 1v1, try to disengage, you usually cannot win.
Get Seeker's Armguard very quickly and try to kill him together with your jungler after he uses his W to trade. Spamping your sidelanes when he starts to roam.
His poke is annoying but that's about it. Try to match his push with your W to prevent him from damaging your tower too much. Get early boots to dodge his poke.

The Zoe matchup is a mixed bag. You counter her E pretty hard, but she can simply run you down with her passive, short ranged Qs and her W. Whenever she ults, try to aim your Q at her initial position to hit her when she returns to it. Get an early Verdant Barrier.

Ask for ganks. Vex, the biggest problem for every assassin. She can use most of her kit to counter your dash, it will result in getting stopped mid dash by her passive fear. Using E around her also gives her extra damage.
He will zone you out. You will not win an early game fight against him. All you can do is try to catch on to his mistakes and punish. Only go in on him if his stun grenade is down.

Hard to out-trade because of the range vs melee situation. He will likely swing away from you if you get on top of him. He will poke you down with his Q early on, try to avoid this if possible. It will help against early trades.
Annie is a good champion against melee assassins, especially since her e will take out your pack really quickly. Most importantly, dont engage when she has her stun up.

Problem is once you've gone in, you cant get out anymore. she can cancel your W with her W. This will put you in an awkward position when trying to get out, since she can chase with Q+E. Try wait for her W to be down.

Fizz most likely dodges all your engages with his e, after his e he will exit the fight with an q, or the other way around. All you can do is wait for mistakes on his part and then punish him in hard.

Lissandra will use q's to poke you from a distance, which will delete your packmates. Avoid this. Be careful for her level 6 since, she will out-trade you if she gets on your first. Make her R herself, rather than you.
She deletes your packmates with one Q, so don't let her get a cantered Q on you. Her push back also counters your W, so wait for her to use her E aggressively and miss on you, then go in.
His ult counters your engage. Plus he has an easy escape, since he can jump over walls making sure you cant follow, also his w is harder to dodge because you are melee.
He has ranged poke, you only have all in melee damage. I'd recommend poking him down with Q then attempt an all-in when his W is down.
Her Q will delete your packmates if it hits. Don't let her E you. You cant go in if her E is up, so bait it out and jump in for her.
Try not to take too much poke damage from her early on, and avoid her charm when initiating. Use your W when charm is down for easy engage.
Mostly a skill matchup. She will try to bully you off the farm, main objective is to not get hit by her e, because she will win the trade if she hits it.
A skill based matchup, as long as you avoid her passive daggers you should be able to win the trades. Just be aware that you should be able to get out of her ult once she hits level 6.

Try to get her passive down as soon as possible (possibly with junglers help). She will use her Q to stun you while you try to engage as you are easy to hit at that point. Try to bait out her stun and you will likely win the trade.
Not that hard, he will likely outrange you a lot and poke you with Q. He will use his ult to get you off him. Try to find gaps and punish on mistakes.
Skill matchup. Don't initiate when he has his E up. He can prevent your W by fearing you when you go in. You do have an advantage at level 6 and a better all in.
Take advantage of when her W is on cooldown. You can use your W to then initiate and if she tries to chain you, it will most likely hit your packmates instead. Be careful of her 6 though.

Make sure to buy Quicksilver Sash at some point in the game and malzahar wont be a problem anymore. Just be careful during laning phase since he will lock you down for his jungler with his ult. Wait for him to use cooldowns on minions and jump on him.
Orianna will make sure to keep you from farming. Go in after she uses her shield and you are most likely to win the trade. The most difficult part is avoiding her ult.

Make sure not to stand close to a wall. Our W is an counter to her stealth, cuz after you reach her she is revealed for 1.5 seconds, meaning she cant go hide in stealth for that duration. After the reveal ends, back off and go in again with w to not get punished by her stealth.
Always take ignite in this matchup. He will try to clear out your pets as soon as possible with all his AoE effects, so try to prevent that from happening and you will win this matchup.

He cant make much use of your ult, Though it is Sylas, he can still out-sustain you. Go for all in's when he's a little above half hp, you should be able to kill him at this point. Don't do all in trades when he's full health, unless you're willing to take his full trade potential.

Your Packmates will actually help with empowering her E. Her E+Q combo can also take out all your packmates and deal some serious damage to you as well, make sure to dodge her E at all times and the matchup will be won.
The most difficult part of this matchup is Veigars cage. You cant go in if he still has it up. Make sure to bait it out, wait for it to be gone and then engage. That is your only win condition.
A pretty skill-based match up. He can use his Q shield and stun to make it difficult for you to engage on him. But a longer fight should be in your advantage, since you can use your E to dodge his W.

Always take Ignite against Vlad. It might be difficult to get him low with all his healing, and his pool might counter your all in, but you will win with the damage output. Just make sure to back off when he has his enhanced Q, (when he has a full red bar)

A fair 1v1 fight in the river would certainly be in your favour. Xerath has the bonus of having huge range. He zones you out of farming, and you cant really engage on him because he most likely hugs his tower. Take advantage when he decides to overextend without his E up.
Dodge his Q tornado, and try to punish him for making dashing mistakes. Don't let him block your Q with wind wall, this cuts your damage in half. Bait it out first before fully committing.
Dodge Q knock-ups. And try not to let him W you too often. If he's using his E kite him out, and when he's just about to go back, follow him with W and all in.
Aurelion will most likely loose an all in from you. He will rely on pushing you in and roam. Find an opening and send him back to base.

He is not really a threat in lane. Avoid getting punished by auto attacks and Q's and all in him whenever you can, he will use his w to get out, but do this over and over and he cant really do much against it.
Not too hard of a matchup. Just don't let her jump on you first, since trading won't be as effective. Her W + passive combo will delete your packmates.
Avoid getting poked by his q and avoid his w stun. overall you will win an all in, just make sure not to be in his blast radius of his ult after 6.
Galio is good against AP, you're AD. All you need to do is avoid getting poked by his q and dodge his charge. after that, he is all yours.

The most difficult part of this matchup is not get hit by her constant e's. Engage as soon as she used her snare and the fight is yours. Last thing to keep an eye on is keeping distance once she hits her e early. The auto attack after deals more damage then the E itself.
Early stage of the game he can kite you out a bit, don't get punished too hard and later on in the game you will slow him enough that he won't be able to kite you.
As long as you can avoid her W+E combo she will be easy to take out.
Velkoz needs to rely mostly on hitting his E. Dodge that and your golden. An added bonus is, that Velkoz usually relies on hitting Q early game, and your pets can tank those hits for you.
He will likely use his W whenever you go in on him, But try to dodge most of his Qs and you will still win most all ins.
Try to avoid his q's, go all in when his slowing wall is down and the fight is yours.
Go hard on him as soon as possible. He will not be able to do alot vs you. just be careful not overextend when his jungler could be around.
You will not have trouble dealing with this guy. If you do have the rare occasion of facing an good Twisted fate, then you should buy an QSS and he wont be able to do anything against you.

Poke and Harass: Early levels are crucial. Use Neeko's range advantage to poke and harass Viktor, especially before he upgrades his abilities. Viktor can struggle in the early game, so zoning and trading effectively can set him behind. Exploit Mobility: Neeko has more mobility than Viktor. Use this advantage to dodge his skill shots, especially his E (Laser), and try to engage when his abilities are on cooldown or if he misuses them. Roaming and Map Pressure: Neeko has good roaming potential due to her crowd control and burst. Push the wave and roam to help other lanes or assist your jungler in invades or skirmishes. Awareness of Viktor's Power Spikes: Be cautious about Viktor's power spikes, particularly when he upgrades his Hex Core and reaches level 6. His damage and utility significantly increase at these points, so adjust your play accordingly.

Level 1 Dominance: Try to establish lane dominance from level 1. Use your range advantage to poke Irelia with auto attacks and abilities. Contest the minion wave to prevent her from stacking her passive (Ionian Fervor). Watch the Minion Wave: Irelia can quickly reset her Q (Bladesurge) by dashing to low-health minions. Be mindful of her positioning concerning the minions and try not to allow her to freely dash around. Consider Building Seeker's Armguard: If Irelia becomes a significant threat, Seeker's Armguard (part of Zhonya's Hourglass) can help mitigate her physical damage and offer some survivability.

Zed's high mobility, especially with his Living Shadow (W), enables him to dodge Neeko's skill shots and close the gap swiftly. His burst damage and potential to outmaneuver Neeko in 1v1 situations make him a tough matchup

Poke and Harass: Cho'Gath's early game sustain relies on his passive, Carnivore, which helps him regenerate health upon killing units. Use Neeko's range advantage to poke Cho'Gath with abilities like her Q (Blooming Burst) while he goes for last hits, forcing him to use his health sustain to recover. Dodge Rupture (Q) and Feral Scream (W): Cho'Gath's main crowd control and damage abilities are his Q (Rupture) and W (Feral Scream). Both are skillshots, so try to anticipate and dodge them. Being hit by these abilities can lead to a significant loss in health or being locked down. Utilize Neeko's Passive: Neeko's passive can be used to deceive Cho'Gath. Utilize it to keep him guessing your positioning, potentially baiting out his abilities or making him play more defensively.

Abuse Neeko's Range: Neeko has good poke potential with her abilities, especially her Q (Blooming Burst). Use this to your advantage by poking Akshan from a safe distance whenever he goes in for last hits or tries to engage. Keep in mind, Akshan's range is limited, so take advantage of your longer range. Engage Wisely: Neeko's E (Tangle-Barbs) can root Akshan in place, giving you an opportunity to follow up with damage. However, be cautious as Akshan can quickly reposition himself using his grappling hook (E). Try to predict his movement or wait for him to use it before engaging. Control Minion Waves: Manipulating the minion wave can help you maintain a safe farming space and make it harder for Akshan to engage on you. Try to keep the wave closer to your turret to limit his all-ins.

Dodge Noxious Blasts (Q) and Twin Fangs (E): Cassiopeia's Q and E abilities are her primary sources of damage. Avoid getting hit by her Q as it will trigger her bonus damage and make it easier for her to land her E. Side-step or move unpredictably to dodge her skillshots.

onsider Roaming: If you find it challenging to win the lane directly, consider roaming to other lanes. Neeko has strong ganking potential with her crowd control abilities and can influence other parts of the map. Build Adaptations: Consider building items that provide magic penetration or burst damage to chip away at Ahri's health. Morellonomicon or Liandry's Torment can be effective choices to mitigate her sustain.

Dodge Paddle Star (Q) and Sleepy Trouble Bubble (E): Zoe's main sources of damage are her Q and E abilities. Dodge her Paddle Star by moving unpredictably, and be extra cautious about her Sleepy Trouble Bubble, as getting hit by it can set her up for a damaging combo. Utilize your movement to sidestep or dodge these skillshots.

Predict Katarina's Movements: Katarina needs to get close to deal damage, so use your E (Tangle-Barbs) skill to predict her movements. Amumu poses a moderate threat in 1v1 situations due to his crowd control and sustained damage from his tantrum. However, he lacks significant burst damage compared to other junglers. Applied Strategies: Invade his jungle early to set him behind and deny him farm. Dodge his Bandage Toss to avoid getting caught out of position. Counter-gank to punish his attempts at initiating fights. Maintain vision control to track his movements and prevent surprise engagements. Engage in skirmishes when his ultimate, Curse of the Sad Mummy, is on cooldown to exploit his vulnerability.

Ekko's mobility and burst damage make him a formidable opponent in 1v1 situations. His ability to rewind time with his ultimate, combined with crowd control from his W, can turn fights in his favor. Applied Strategies: Predict his movement to dodge his skill shots. Engage when his crowd control abilities are on cooldown. Control vision to limit his roaming potential. Counter-gank to punish his aggressive plays. Focus on securing objectives to maintain map control.

Elise excels in early duels with her high burst damage and crowd control from her Cocoon ability. She can quickly burst down squishy targets and outmaneuver opponents with her mobility. Applied Strategies: Avoid getting caught by her Cocoon ability by juking and using mobility spells. Counter-gank to turn the tide of fights in your favor, as Elise's early-game strength relies heavily on successful ganks. Ward her jungle entrances to track her movements and anticipate her gank paths. Engage in extended fights where her burst damage is less effective, especially if she misses her Cocoon. Utilize vision control to deny her vision and limit her map presence.

Evelynn's strength lies in her ability to catch opponents off guard with her stealth and burst damage. In 1v1 situations, she can quickly burst down targets with her Hate Spike ability and Allure charm. Applied Strategies: Invest in vision control to track Evelynn's movements and anticipate her gank paths, as she relies heavily on stealth for her engages. Avoid face-checking bushes or isolated areas where Evelynn may be lurking. Engage in team fights where Evelynn's squishiness and lack of crowd control make her vulnerable. Build magic resistance to mitigate Evelynn's burst damage, as she primarily deals magic damage. Coordinate with your team to collapse on Evelynn when she engages or attempts to flank during team fights.

Fiddlesticks excels in extended fights due to his sustain from Drain and crowd control from Fear. Engaging him in a 1v1 situation can be challenging due to his ability to fear and silence opponents while draining their health. Applied Strategies: Avoid prolonged engagements with Fiddlesticks, as his sustain from Drain can outlast many opponents. Interrupt Fiddlesticks' Drain channel with crowd control abilities or by moving out of range. Prioritize vision control to prevent Fiddlesticks from ambushing with his Crowstorm ultimate. Coordinate with your team to focus Fiddlesticks in team fights, as he is susceptible to burst damage when caught out of position. Build magic resistance to mitigate Fiddlesticks' damage output, as he primarily deals magic damage.

Gragas poses a moderate threat in 1v1 situations due to his ability to displace opponents with Body Slam and deal significant burst damage with his explosive barrels. His crowd control abilities also make him challenging to deal with in close combat. Applied Strategies: Avoid fighting Gragas in narrow spaces where his explosive barrels can easily hit multiple targets. Watch out for Gragas' Body Slam, which can be used to engage or disengage from fights. Try to anticipate its usage and position accordingly. Be mindful of Gragas' ultimate ability, Explosive Cask, which can disrupt your positioning and scatter your team in team fights. Position yourself away from walls to minimize its impact. Take advantage of Gragas' relatively long cooldowns early in the game. Look for opportunities to engage when his abilities are on cooldown. Consider building health and magic resistance items to withstand Gragas' burst damage and sustain longer in fights.

Graves is a formidable duelist with high burst damage and sustained damage output, especially in close-range skirmishes. His Quickdraw ability allows him to kite opponents effectively while dealing significant damage with his shotgun shells. Additionally, Graves can quickly stack his True Grit passive, granting him bonus armor and magic resist in extended fights. Applied Strategies: Be cautious when engaging Graves in 1v1 situations, especially in close quarters where he can maximize the damage from his shotgun shells. Respect Graves' burst potential, particularly when he has accumulated multiple stacks of his True Grit passive. Look for opportunities to disengage if you are at risk of being overwhelmed. Utilize crowd control effects to disrupt Graves' movement and prevent him from freely kiting or repositioning during fights. Prioritize vision control and map awareness to track Rengar's movements and anticipate his gank paths and jungle routes. Communicate with your team to coordinate counter-ganks and defensive plays to thwart Rengar's engage attempts and turn the tide of the fight in your favor. Use crowd control and burst damage to lock down Rengar and prevent him from escaping or repositioning during fights. Build defensively against Rengar's burst damage and assassination potential, prioritizing items that offer health, resistances, or crowd control reduction. Stay grouped with your team and maintain proper spacing to prevent Rengar from catching you out with his engage tools. Punish Rengar for overextending or mispositioning in fights and skirmishes, taking advantage of his limited mobility and vulnerability to crowd control effects. Coordinate with your team to collapse on Rengar and focus him down quickly before he can dish out significant damage or escape.

Additionally, Shaco's clone from Hallucinate (R) adds an extra layer of confusion and unpredictability to duels, making it difficult for Nocturne to accurately target the real Shaco. Applied Strategies: Prioritize vision control and map awareness to track Shaco's movements and anticipate his gank paths and jungle routes. Place wards in key areas of the map, such as river entrances, jungle camps, and objective pits, to spot Shaco's approach and avoid falling victim to his ambushes. Play defensively and cautiously in the early game, as Shaco excels at invading enemy junglers and securing early kills to snowball ahead. Avoid overextending in the jungle or pushing aggressively without vision, as Shaco can punish isolated targets and capitalize on positional mistakes. Communicate with your team to coordinate counter-ganks and defensive plays to thwart Shaco's engage attempts and turn the tide of the fight in your favor. Use crowd control and burst damage to lock down Shaco and prevent him from escaping or repositioning during fights. Build defensively against Shaco's burst damage and assassination potential, prioritizing items that offer health, resistances, or crowd control reduction. Shyvana presents a moderate challenge for Nocturne in the jungle, particularly in 1v1 scenarios. Shyvana boasts high sustained damage and dueling potential, especially when she's in her dragon form. Her Twin Bite (Q) ability allows her to quickly shred through enemy champions and jungle monsters, while her Burnout (W) provides her with increased movement speed and area-of-effect damage in fights. Additionally, Shyvana's Dragon's Descent (R) transforms her into a fearsome dragon, granting her bonus stats and empowering her abilities, making her a formidable foe for Nocturne to face head-on. Applied Strategies: Capitalize on Shyvana's weak early game by applying pressure and contesting objectives in the early stages of the match. Shyvana tends to struggle with early game ganks and skirmishes, especially before she acquires her core items and levels up her abilities. Take advantage of this window of opportunity to secure early kills, deny her farm, and establish vision control over key areas of the map. Play around Shyvana's cooldowns and resource management, particularly her Dragon's Descent (R) ultimate ability. Keep track of the cooldown timer on Shyvana's ultimate and look for opportunities to engage or disengage when it's on cooldown. Without access to her ultimate, Shyvana loses a significant portion of her dueling and teamfighting power, allowing Nocturne to capitalize on her vulnerability. Prioritize counter-jungling and invading Shyvana's jungle to set her behind and disrupt her farming patterns. Shyvana relies heavily on farming jungle camps to scale into the late game, so denying her access to her camps and starving her of resources can significantly impact her power spikes and scaling potential. Look for opportunities to steal her buffs, contest scuttle crabs, and punish her for overextending in the jungle. Build defensively against Shyvana's mixed damage output and scaling potential, prioritizing items that offer health, armor, or magic resistance. Consider investing in items like Randuin's Omen or Spirit Visage to mitigate Shyvana's physical and magic damage and increase your survivability in fights. Adapt your itemization based on Shyvana's build path and team composition, focusing on countering her strengths and neutralizing her threat. Coordinate with your team to secure objectives and maintain map pressure throughout the game, denying Shyvana opportunities to split push or farm uncontested. Contest dragon spawns, secure Rift Herald, and prioritize turret plates to maintain control over the map and limit Shyvana's ability to scale into the late game. By maintaining objective control and map pressure, you can prevent Shyvana from reaching her full potential and secure victory for your team.

Skarner poses a moderate challenge for Nocturne in 1v1 situations due to his sustained damage, crowd control, and dueling potential. Skarner's Crystal Slash (Q) ability allows him to consistently deal damage to his targets while also lowering the cooldown of his other abilities. Additionally, his Fracture (E) ability provides him with sustain and a slowing effect, making it difficult for Nocturne to escape or kite him effectively. Furthermore, Skarner's Impale (R) ultimate ability can suppress and drag Nocturne away from safety, potentially turning the tide of a fight in Skarner's favor. Applied Strategies: Exploit Skarner's weaknesses in the early game by pressuring him and contesting objectives to limit his farming and scaling potential. Skarner typically requires time to scale into the late game and relies heavily on farming jungle camps to reach his power spikes. By denying him access to his jungle camps and contesting objectives like scuttle crabs and dragon spawns, you can set him behind and disrupt his momentum. Be mindful of Skarner's Crystal Spires on the map, as they empower his abilities and grant him increased movement speed and attack speed while he's within their range. Avoid fighting Skarner near his Crystal Spires whenever possible, as he gains a significant advantage when fighting within their influence. Instead, look for opportunities to engage or skirmish in areas where Skarner's mobility is limited, such as narrow pathways or jungle corridors. Prioritize building Tenacity and defensive items against Skarner's crowd control and sustained damage output. Items like Mercury's Treads and Sterak's Gage can help mitigate the impact of Skarner's crowd control abilities and provide you with increased survivability in fights. Adapt your itemization based on Skarner's build path and team composition, focusing on countering his strengths and neutralizing his threat. Coordinate with your team to kite and peel for each other during teamfights and skirmishes, particularly when Skarner is looking to engage with his Impale (R) ultimate ability. Position yourself strategically and use crowd control abilities to disrupt Skarner's engages and prevent him from reaching priority targets. By effectively kiting and peeling for each other, you can mitigate Skarner's impact in teamfights and turn the tide of battle in your favor. Maintain vision control over key areas of the map and be proactive in denying Skarner opportunities to engage or flank your team. Ward entrances to your jungle, objectives like dragon and Baron, and choke points in the river to spot Skarner's movements and anticipate his engages. By maintaining vision control and denying Skarner opportunities to catch your team off guard, you can neutralize his threat and maintain control over the map.

Facing Trundle as Nocturne in a 1v1 scenario poses a significant challenge due to Trundle's strong dueling potential and sustain from his passive, King's Tribute. Trundle excels in extended fights thanks to his ability to steal stats with Subjugate (R), making him tankier and stronger while simultaneously weakening his opponents. Additionally, his Pillar of Ice (E) can disrupt Nocturne's mobility and positioning, hindering his ability to stick to targets or disengage effectively. Applied Strategies: Avoid prolonged engagements with Trundle whenever possible, especially when his Subjugate (R) is active. Trundle gains significant bonus stats and sustain while his ultimate is active, making him incredibly difficult to duel. Instead, look for quick burst trades or coordinated engages with your team to burst down Trundle before he can sustain through the damage. Utilize Nocturne's spell shield to negate the effects of Trundle's Pillar of Ice (E) and prevent being disrupted during engagements. Trundle's Pillar of Ice can interrupt Nocturne's spell casts or impede his movement, so timing your spell shield to block this ability can be crucial in maintaining your momentum during fights. Coordinate with your team to kite and peel for each other during teamfights to mitigate Trundle's effectiveness. Trundle excels in close-quarters combat and thrives on isolating targets with his Pillar of Ice, so staying grouped and utilizing crowd control effects to peel for each other can neutralize his threat and allow your team to focus him down. Take advantage of Trundle's lack of mobility and reliance on Pillar of Ice to engage or disengage fights. Trundle has limited mobility and no dashes or blinks in his kit, so he can struggle to escape from sticky situations or disengage from unfavorable fights. Exploit this weakness by engaging on Trundle when he's out of position or punishing him for overextending in fights. Build items like Blade of the Ruined King or Lord Dominik's Regards to shred through Trundle's high health pool and sustain. Trundle's strength lies in his tankiness and ability to steal stats, so building items that provide bonus damage based on enemy health or armor penetration can help cut through his defenses and secure kills more efficiently. Maintain vision control around objectives and key areas of the map to prevent Trundle from flanking or setting up picks with his Pillar of Ice. Trundle's Pillar of Ice can create terrain obstacles that disrupt enemy movement and split up teams, so having vision of potential flank routes or choke points can help your team anticipate his engages and respond accordingly.

Facing Udyr as Nocturne in a 1v1 scenario presents a moderate challenge due to Udyr's strong early game dueling and sustained damage output. Udyr's kit revolves around rapidly cycling through his stances to enhance his basic attacks and abilities, allowing him to quickly burst down targets or kite them effectively. Additionally, Udyr's Bear Stance (E) provides him with a powerful stun that can interrupt Nocturne's engages or disengages, potentially turning the tide of skirmishes in his favor. Utilize Nocturne's spell shield to block Udyr's crowd control effects and mitigate his damage output during trades or engages. Timing your spell shield to absorb Udyr's Bear Stance stun or Tiger Stance (Q) enhanced basic attacks can prevent you from being locked down and bursted down quickly, giving you an opportunity to counterattack or disengage safely. Nocturne's ability to stick to targets with Duskbringer (Q) and fear them with Unspeakable Horror (E) can make it difficult for Udyr to reach and stick to priority targets, allowing you to outmaneuver him and poke him down from range. Coordinate with your team to peel for each other and focus down Udyr during teamfights to neutralize his threat. Udyr's strength lies in his ability to single out targets and burst them down quickly with his Tiger Stance (Q) and Phoenix Stance (R) combos, so staying grouped and protecting each other with crowd control effects and shields can mitigate his impact on fights and turn the tide in your favor. Build items like Blade of the Ruined King or Black Cleaver to shred through Udyr's health and armor, allowing you to deal more damage and cut through his tankiness more effectively. Udyr typically builds tanky items like Sunfire Aegis or Frostfire Gauntlet to enhance his durability and survivability, so building items that provide bonus damage based on enemy health or armor penetration can help you overcome his defenses and secure kills more efficiently. Control vision around objectives and key areas of the map to track Udyr's movements and prevent him from sneaking objectives or setting up picks with his team. Udyr's high mobility and map presence make him a potent threat in the jungle, so maintaining vision control and denying him opportunities to flank or ambush your team can limit his impact on the game and allow you to dictate the pace of play.
